extracted.intended_audience: DoD contracting officers, defense contractors/offerors, small business stakeholders, and members of the public interested in DFARS threshold rulemaking and submitting comments
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed DFARS rule implementing 41 U.S.C. 1908 to adjust acquisition-related dollar thresholds for inflation (using CPI), amending numerous DFARS parts and inviting public comments by a specified deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments on the proposed rule should be submitted in writing on or before March 18, 2025, to be considered in the formation of the final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit comments identified by DFARS Case 2024-D002 using Regulations.gov (search DFARS Case 2024-D002 and select 'Comment') or email osd.dfars@mail.mil with DFARS Case 2024-D002 in subject. Comments generally will be posted without change to regulations.gov; check posting ~2–3 days after submission to verify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment submission methods and posting policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments may be submitted via the Federal eRulemaking Portal (regulations.gov) or by email; comments received generally will be posted without change, including any personal information provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the case number on attached documents; confirm receipt by checking regulations.gov 2–3 days after submission. Be aware comments may be publicly viewable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of acquisition-related threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: "Acquisition-related threshold" means a dollar threshold specified in law, Executive order, or regulation as a factor defining the scope of applicability of a policy, procedure, requirement, or restriction to procurement of property or services by an Executive agency—generally tied to contract, subcontract, or modification value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This interpretation builds on prior DFARS reviews (2005, 2010, 2015, 2020). Thresholds not specified in law but meeting the other criteria (e.g., based in Executive order or regulation) are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory requirement to adjust thresholds (41 U.S.C. 1908)
rubrics_metrics.description: 41 U.S.C. 1908 requires adjustment every five years (on Oct. 1 of years evenly divisible by five) of statutory acquisition-related thresholds for inflation using the Consumer Price Index for all urban consumers (CPI-U).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statute prescribes inflation adjustment methodology for statutory thresholds except specifically excluded categories (see exceptions). DoD proposes to apply same methodology to some nonstatutory DFARS thresholds as a policy matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories excluded from escalation under statute
rubrics_metrics.description: The statute does not permit escalation of thresholds established by the Construction Wage Rate Requirements statute (Davis-Bacon Act), the Service Contract Labor Standards statute, performance and payment bonds (formerly the Miller Act), or trade agreements thresholds (USTR/Trade Agreements Act of 1979).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also, thresholds originating in Executive order or implementing agency regulations cannot be escalated unless those Executive orders or agency regulations are amended first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation method for statutory thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Escalation is calculated using the CPI for all urban consumers: projected CPI for March 2025 (323.193) divided by the CPI for the date of enactment of the statute or regulation (October 2000 for statutes enacted prior to Oct. 1, 2000).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DoD will adjust calculations if actual March 2025 CPI differs from the projection prior to final rule issuance. The matrix on regulations.gov identifies original statutory thresholds and subsequent revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rounding rules for escalated statutory thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: After applying the escalation factor, statutory thresholds must be rounded by specified bins: <$10,000 nearest $500; $10,000-<$100,000 nearest $5,000; $100,000-<$1M nearest $50,000; $1M-<$10M nearest $500,000; $10M-<$100M nearest $5M; $100M-<$1B nearest $50M; $1B+ nearest $500M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because prior escalated amounts were rounded in 2020, calculations here are based on base year amounts (not the rounded 2020 escalated amounts) to avoid distortion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use base-year amounts for calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculations in this proposed rule are based on the base year amount (original statutory/regulatory amount) because escalated amounts in 2020 were subject to rounding which would distort future calculations if used as the base.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This produces consistent escalation across review periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation for some thresholds not changing
rubrics_metrics.description: Some thresholds subject to inflation calculation in 2020 did not change because inflation was insufficient to overcome rounding; similarly, some thresholds that escalated in 2020 may not escalate in 2025 while others that did not escalate in 2020 may increase due to additional inflation or statutory changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actual escalation depends on CPI and rounding; projected CPI may cause additional thresholds to escalate in final rule if higher than projected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy-based (nonstatutory) DFARS thresholds escalation recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: No statutory authorization is required to escalate policy-based (nonstatutory) DFARS thresholds; DoD generally recommends applying the same escalation formula to these thresholds unless a reason is provided not to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is for consistency between statutory and policy thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability to SAT, commercial products, and commercial services
rubrics_metrics.description: This proposed rule amends certain DFARS provisions and clauses but does not impose new requirements on contracts at or below the Simplified Acquisition Threshold (SAT), on commercial products (including COTS items), or on commercial services; it does not change applicability of provisions/clauses to those acquisitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affected DFARS clauses include 252.204-7007 Alt A; 252.215-7016; 252.216-7010; 252.225-7003, but the rule does not broaden applicability to below-SAT or commercial acquisitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected impact — maintain status quo / minimal economic impact
rubrics_metrics.description: DoD does not expect the finalized rule to have a significant impact because the rule is intended to maintain the status quo by adjusting thresholds for inflation; accordingly, the rule is not a significant regulatory action under E.O. 12866.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DoD performed an initial Regulatory Flexibility Analysis and concluded minimal impact on a substantial number of small entities; invites comments from small businesses on expected impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Orders 12866 and 13563 review statement
rubrics_metrics.description: E.O.s 12866 and 13563 direct agencies to assess costs/benefits and select approaches that maximize net benefits; this proposed rule is not a significant regulatory action and was not subject to review under section 6(b) of E.O. 12866.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.O. 13563 emphasizes quantification of costs/benefits, reducing costs, harmonization, and promoting flexibility — used as analytic context even though this action is not significant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Act (RFA) analysis summary and invitation
rubrics_metrics.description: An initial regulatory flexibility analysis indicates the proposed rule will have a minimal economic impact on a substantial number of small entities; DoD invites comments from small business concerns and other interested parties on the expected impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments concerning existing regulations in affected subparts should cite 5 U.S.C. 610 (DFARS Case 2024-D002).

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The changes do not impose additional information collection requirements beyond previously approved paperwork burdens (OMB Control Nos. 9000-0189 and 0704-0229).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DoD cites the existing OMB approvals covering affected FAR and DFARS sections/clauses.

rubrics_metrics.name: 203.1004 threshold amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend 203.1004(b)(2)(ii): remove "$6 million" and add "$7.5 million".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a specific DFARS numeric threshold change implementing the CPI escalation/rounding.

rubrics_metrics.name: 205.303 announcement of contract awards threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise 205.303(a)(i): "The threshold for DoD awards is $9.5 million. Report all contractual actions, including modifications, that have a face value, excluding unexercised options, of more than $9.5 million."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance for reporting undefinitized actions and indefinite delivery contracts is included (report NTE for undefinitized; for ID/I/C contracts, report initial award if estimated face value excluding options is >$9.5M; do not report orders up to estimated value).

rubrics_metrics.name: 206.303-1 and 206.303-2 threshold amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend 206.303-1 and 206.303-2 by removing "$100 million" and adding "$150 million" in applicable paragraphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These increase thresholds used in competition/justification rules and related provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 206.304 threshold amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend 206.304 (paragraph (a)(S-71) introductory text) by removing "$100 million" and adding "$150 million".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the cluster of competition threshold adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: 209.409 threshold amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend 209.409 by removing "$150,000" and adding "$200,000".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contractor qualifications threshold change.

rubrics_metrics.name: 211.503 threshold amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend 211.503(b) by removing "$750,000" wherever it appears and adding "$950,000" in its place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes thresholds tied to acquisition-solicitation/contracting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: 212.271 threshold amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend 212.271 by removing "$45,000" and adding "$55,000".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjusts the DFARS threshold related to acquisition of commercial products/services paperwork.

rubrics_metrics.name: 215.403-1 threshold amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend 215.403-1(c)(4)(B) by removing "$20 million" and adding "$25 million".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affects thresholds in contracting by negotiation guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: 215.506 postaward debriefing requirement (threshold)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend 215.506(b): a written or oral debriefing is required for contract awards valued at $15 million or more (notwithstanding FAR 15.506(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This implements section 818 of the National Defense Authorization Act for FY2018; further disclosure rules for different award sizes are in 215.506(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: 215.506 disclosure rules for source selection decision document
rubrics_metrics.description: For contracts >$15M and ≤$150M with a small business or nontraditional defense contractor, offeror may request disclosure of agency's written source selection decision document (SSDD) redacted to protect other offerors' confidential/proprietary info; for contracts >$150M, disclose SSDD (redacted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Redaction must protect confidential/proprietary information of other offerors.

rubrics_metrics.name: 215.570 threshold amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend 215.570 by removing "$10 million" and adding "$15 million".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjusts threshold referenced in this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: 216.505 ordering / postaward debriefing for orders threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend 216.505(b)(6): Postaward notices and debriefing of awardees for orders — a written or oral postaward debriefing of successful and unsuccessful awardees is required for task orders and delivery orders valued at $15 million or more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow procedures at 215.506 and 215.506-70 when providing postaward debriefings for such orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: 216.506-70 threshold amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend 216.506-70(b) by removing "$10 million" and adding "$15 million".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aligns task-order debriefing thresholds with other DFARS changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: 217.170/217.171/217.172 threshold amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend 217.170 (change $150M to $200M in specified paragraphs), 217.171 (change $750M to $950M), and 217.172 (change $750M to $950M in listed paragraphs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These change special contracting methods thresholds and dollar-value limits for various authorities/exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 219.502-2 and 219.808-1 small business thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend 219.502-2: paragraph (1) change $3 million to $3.5 million; paragraph (2) change $1.5 million to $2 million. Amend 219.808-1(a) by removing "$100 million" and adding "$150 million".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjusts small business program thresholds used for set-aside/solicitation size standards and related requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: 225 (Foreign Acquisition) cluster threshold amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple amendments in Part 225 updating dollar thresholds — e.g., change $1.5M to $2M in 225.103; change $150,000 to $200,000 in 225.771-2 and 225.771-5 and 225.7002-2 and 225.7023-3 and 225.7023-4; change $750,000 to $950,000 in 225.7201; change $15M to $20M in 225.7204; change $100M to $150M in 225.7703-2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are specific numeric updates to foreign acquisition thresholds and reporting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: 236.303-1 and 236.601 construction thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend 236.303-1: change $4.5M to $5.5M; amend 236.601(1): change $1.5M to $2M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Updates construction and architect-engineer contract thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: 237.170-2 service contracting threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend 237.170-2(a)(1) and (2) by removing "$100 million" and adding "$150 million".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjusts thresholds for service contracting special authorities/exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 246.402 quality assurance threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend 246.402 introductory text by removing "$350,000" and adding "$400,000".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Updates the threshold used in quality-assurance-related provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 250.102-1 extraordinary contractual actions threshold
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Updates threshold for extraordinary contractual actions and related DFARS provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 252.204-7007 Alternate A representation threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend 252.204-7007 Alternate A: revise provision date and in paragraph (d)(1)(v) remove "$150,000" and add "$200,000".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Updates annual representations and certifications alternate provision dollar threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: 252.215-7016 Notification to Offerors—Postaward Debriefings (timing and content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise 252.215-7016: Government will provide written or oral postaward debriefing upon timely request to successful/unsuccessful offerors for contract awards valued at $15M or more; timely request = within 3 days of notification of contract award. Minimum postaward debriefing information includes SSDD disclosure options (see thresholds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If debriefing is provided, the debriefed offeror may submit additional written questions within 2 business days; agency will respond within 5 business days; debriefing not concluded until delivery or until agency delivers its written response to timely additional questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 252.216-7010 Postaward Debriefings for Task Orders/Delivery Orders threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise 252.216-7010 clause date and change paragraph (a)(1) by removing "$10 million" and adding "$15 million".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aligns task-order/debriefing thresholds with other DFARS sections requiring debriefings at $15M or more.

rubrics_metrics.name: 252.225-7003 Report of Intended Performance Outside U.S./Canada threshold and reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise 252.225-7003 paragraph (b): Offeror shall submit with its offer a report of intended performance outside U.S./Canada if (1) the offer exceeds $20 million in value; and (2) the Offeror is aware that the Offeror or a first-tier subcontractor intends to perform any part of the contract outside U.S./Canada that (i) exceeds $950,000 in value; and (ii) could be performed inside the U.S. or Canada.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Updates the dollar thresholds for required reporting of intended foreign performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matrix and supporting documents published on regulations.gov
rubrics_metrics.description: A matrix on regulations.gov identifies the statute and statutory threshold (including original threshold and any subsequent revisions) and supporting threshold matrices are provided as supporting documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations.gov docket DARS-2024-0039 contains the Threshold Matrix (published supporting documents) used for transparency and public review.
